data.content_ref: inline:The target claims a Poisson temporal signature distinguishes truly independent failures from hidden correlated failures, but it never supplies the causal mechanism by which a staggered correlated failure (with differing propagation delays across nodes) would remain distinguishable from a Poisson process. Two independent failure processes superposed are themselves Poisson; and a correlated trigger convolved with heterogeneous, independent propagation delays also yields a process that can be indistinguishable from Poisson on the observation window. The target's own countercondition (subtle/delayed trigger smoothing out clustering) concedes the signature can vanish, yet the central claim is stated unconditionally. Since the problem demands we identify what evidence would distinguish the two regimes, a purely descriptive temporal-clustering signature with no causal derivation of why correlated triggers must violate Poisson-distributed arrivals fails the standard.
